label: first original token is q, g, or 2
explanation: Fires on step 0 of the original phase when the first token is q, 2, or g. Every such step is active (dev precision 1.0), and these steps hold about 93% of activation mass. Magnitude depends on the token: q is strongest (about 1.0 of max), then 2 (about 0.45), then g (about 0.36). The remaining roughly 17% of active steps are weaker firings on q at steps 1-3; q there fires only part of the time, so adding that clause lowers F1 (0.75-0.79). Never fires in the delimiter or copy phases, never at t >= 4, and almost never on any other token.

issues: Minor: about 16% of active steps (6.4% of mass) are partial firings on q at t=1-3. Precision there is only 0.15-0.28, and conditioning on prev_tok, to_go, or seen(digits / q,g,2) did not find a cleaner subset. Adding t==2 & q lowers test F1 to 0.863. The explanation already reports this residual honestly.

Checked claims: test precision 1.0, recall 0.829, mass recall 0.934. Zero false positives. No activity in the delimiter or copy phases, none at t>=4, and only 1 test step active on other tokens at t>0. Mean magnitude ratio q:2:g at t=0, worked out from mass/count, is about 1:0.45:0.37, which matches the stated ordering.
